request.deadline: 18-month funding period with milestones from Q3 2026 through 2027
deliverables: Establish or host a not-for-profit entity and publish transition architecture, migration plan, and public usage dashboard in Q3 2026.
Hold a board election via on-chain voting under published rules in Q4 2026.
Serve all public API traffic from the new stack and legally transfer Blockfrost source code, trademarks, domain names, and associated assets to the governing entity in Q1 2027.
Run a public sustainability consultation and publish the chosen long-term direction in Q2-Q3 2027.
Operate the public API at a minimum 99% monthly uptime SLA with quarterly technical and budget reports during 2027.
request.recipient: Input Output / Blockfrost transition administered through Intersect and Cardano Development Holdings arrangements as described in the document
request.what: Fund Blockfrost's transition into a free, community-governed not-for-profit public API for Cardano, including 18 months of transition and operations.

claims.claim: Blockfrost is presented as a reliable hosted REST interface that lets Cardano developers interact with the blockchain without running their own infrastructure or node.
The document states that Blockfrost usage in the Cardano Foundation developer ecosystem survey rose from 39.3% in 2022 to 71.5% in 2025, with links to each annual survey result.
The proposer states that last month Blockfrost served 781k unique visitors, more than 1.84 billion API requests, almost 700 requests per second, and over 7 TB of API data.
The document claims that in most Cardano epochs more than 50% of all transactions are submitted through Blockfrost.
The proposal says more than 100 Icebreakers have joined the effort to decentralize Blockfrost operations.
The proposer claims 90% of all Cardano traffic served through the Blockfrost API comes from the free tier, making the commercial model difficult for financing the public-good operation.

The document commits that all Blockfrost intellectual property, including source code, trademarks, domain names, and associated assets, will be transferred to the governing not-for-profit entity as part of the transition.
The requested budget is 9,832,979 ADA, calculated as 1,868,266 USD at 0.19 USD per ADA, allocated mainly to staffing, operations and infrastructure, and legal/accounting costs.
The proposal says any unspent post-transition infrastructure budget will be returned to the treasury and that quarterly reports will include technical data and a budget summary.

The document states that project delivery, milestone acceptance, contract management, auditable accounts, and fund delegation will be handled through legal contracts, Intersect delivery assurance, third-party assurance, and treasury management smart contracts.

summary: The document requests 9,832,979 ADA for an 18-month transition of Blockfrost into a community-governed not-for-profit public API, citing high developer adoption and transaction-submission importance while providing milestone, governance, reporting, and budget structures but relying on proposer assertions for several key usage and dependency claims.
